subject: Copperleaf landing-zone footprint & encryption alignment
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@copperleaf.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@copperleaf.io>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questions — initial inventory + encryption

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. We’re starting to formalize the on-prem landing-zone for Copperleaf’s inference workloads and I wanted to loop you in early so we can align on requirements before our procurement window next month. A few quick context points:

- Target workload: steady-state 150 qps (text generation) with burst to 450 qps during nightly batch windows.
- Data classification: PII + proprietary financial models — all persisted data must be encrypted at rest and we need proof points for key custody (customer-managed KMS preferred).
- Rack layout: two racks per site, dual-redundant top-of-rack switches, private peering to our VPC via Direct Connect.

Attached is our site inventory spreadsheet (copperleaf-site-inventory-20280425.xlsx) with basic NICs, usable NVMe pool sizes, and expected retention windows. High-level questions we need answered:

1) Recommended node-pool mix for latency-sensitive vs batch tails (GPUs + CPU-only worker ratios).
2) PV class and IO tiers: ephemeral NVMe vs provisioned block; recommended eviction policies for the real-time pools.
3) Encryption at rest & key management integration options for an on-prem private deployment.

Could your team propose a concise topology and a short runbook checklist (network preflight + disk encryption verification) we can use during the procurement/RFP step? We’re aiming to lock hardware by May 15.

Cheers,
Priya Rao
Head of Infrastructure, Copperleaf Systems

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Priya —

Appreciate the detailed inventory. Quick read-through notes below and I attached a short guidance PDF (recommended-nodepool-and-io-matrix.pdf) with the sizing rationale. High-level answers first, then a short checklist: 

1) Node-pool mix
- Real-time: 6x A100-40GB GPUs across two racks (3 per rack) in a continuous-batching pool; pair each GPU node with 2x CPU-only sidecars for preprocessing (request shaping).
- Batch: separate flex pool of GPU-spotable nodes (same instance class) configured for long-tail batching; autoscale target based on queue depth with preemptible margin.
- Infra/control: 3 masters (control plane) on dedicated VMs with local SSD for kube components + etcd replicated across sites (if multi-site).

2) PV / IO tiers
- Ephemeral NVMe for KV cache and token-generation scratch (temp data), use ephemeral local volumes with node-affinity and automatic MVCC tombstone eviction at 24-48h.
- Provisioned block (iSCSI/FC) for long-term model artifacts and customer data; recommend using LVM on top of block store and kube PVs with ReadWriteMany where supported.
- Use two storage classes: fast-io (guaranteed IOPS) and archival (encrypted, lower IOPS).

3) Encryption & KMS
- Support for customer-managed KMS via Redwood Private with KMIP/HSM integration. We can provide an HSM connector; the recommended approach is to hold envelope keys in your KMS and keep disk keys rotated by the cluster-side agent.

Preflight checklist (summary)
- Confirm MTU, BGP peering, and private VLANs established for direct VPC peering.
- Confirm DNS resolution and split-horizon records for internal endpoints.
- Verify hardware NVMe firmware and stable SMART metrics.
- Validate encryption: test key rotation and verify disk rekey without downtime.
- Validate snapshot/restore for model PVs and eviction policy for ephemeral caches.

I’ll loop in Laura and Marissa for the runbook verifications and we’ll draft a one-page procurement playbook you can include in the RFP. Expect the first draft of the procurement checklist + minimal runbook by Thursday.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Karthik —

Uploading the updated inventory (see attached) and a couple clarifying points after running this past our infra team: 

- We have two NVMe tiers: local M.2s (small capacity) and rack-level NVMe arrays (larger pool). We should treat local M.2 as strictly ephemeral.
- Retention requirements: model artifacts must be kept for 60 days; audit logs must be kept for 2 years off-site.
- Key custody: Copperleaf will use AWS KMS in the customer account (key policy allows our on-prem HSM gateway to envelope/decrypt). We need a documented proof path for rotation and audits.

Two follow-ups: 1) Can Redwood provide a short validation test we can run during pilot to prove encryption and rekey workflows? 2) Any special considerations for Direct Connect failover to VPN fallback?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Wallace

ben.wallace@copperleaf.io

Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — initial inventory + encryption

Ben/Priya —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached are three artifacts: 1) recommended-nodepool-and-io-matrix.pdf (sizing + rationale), 2) a one-page procurement playbook with the preflight checklist, and 3) a network-egress-diagram.png that shows Direct Connect + VPN fallback routing. Short answers to your follow-ups below, plus next steps: 

Validation test for encryption/rekey
- We’ll provide a small test harness that: (a) provisions a test PV, (b) writes a known dataset, (c) rotates the envelope key via your KMS, and (d) verifies readability post-rotate. We’ll run the same test in our lab and share the automation steps (expect a GitHub repo link in the playbook).

Direct Connect failover considerations
- Ensure BGP timers are aggressive for failover (BFD optional). On failover to VPN we expect ~100–250ms additional latency; recommend keeping a small warm pool of nodes in a second AZ to handle transition spikes. Also configure egress rules to prefer private peer over VPN and fail open only for non-sensitive telemetry.

Recommended quick topology (summary)
- Two racks, cross-rack pod anti-affinity for real-time pools.
- Real-time GPU pool: 6 GPUs (3 per rack) with local NVMe ephemeral cache; set eviction TTL = 36h default, admission control at 75% cache fill.
- Long-term model store: replicated blockstore with daily snapshots, retention 60 days (objects) and archived to off-site object store for 2y audit logs.

Next steps
- Copperleaf: confirm procurement RFQ date (you mentioned May 15) and whether we should include an HSM appliance in the BOM.
- Redwood: we’ll deliver the draft procurement playbook and the encryption validation repo by Friday EOD.

If that looks good I’ll turn this into a short one-pager you can attach to the RFP.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
